core.text: Host: the existing Endless Museum. Keep museum encounters, tutorial learning and critical-poetic writing as overlapping sets. Teach selected reusable operations; name supplied support. findings.text: Separate the closing Primitives encounters: generated forms / tighter Ignorance -> Godot's supplied mesh forms -> exploration with columns and letter profiles -> Portals (finite approximations and chosen tolerance) -> Melencolia. Retain Coordinates, Trace and Grid in the opening lineage. Give exploration distinct space: first compare one profile at 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16 radial segments, then vary outline and height; use letter profiles to expose inherited outlines, holes and new bodily uses. This is a route proposal, not a changed sequence.
findings.reason: Palle identifies Ignorance as too dense and asks for a clearer exploratory direction. Its current manuscript and map combine the Platonic courtyard, sphere comparisons, cost display, capsule and engine mesh library. The existing Primitives_Godot map is outside the authored sequence. Columns and glyph studies provide concrete material for a separate exploration encounter.
findings.sequence_effect: Let construction, borrowed engine forms, artistic choices, limits and meaning have distinct moments. The column lesson can reuse lists, loops and a supplied sampler; the glyph geometry builder can remain supplied. Do not imply that arbitrary profile sweeps are built-in PrimitiveMesh types. Pi is finite; an endless decimal expansion, polygon convergence and a philosophical ideal are distinct. Do not turn Melencolia into another syntax lesson.
findings.project_effect: Use sequence review to redistribute attention while preserving the wider artifact ecology. Keep the source-supported inventory separate from the curatorial judgment and a future VR assessment. Do not force every object into a tutorial or remove older works just to match a reduced summary.
